newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Up to 100,000 refugees in Tanzania head for Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Up to 100,000 refugees in Tanzania head for Rwanda.

text.p: Up to 100,000 weary and ragged Rwandan refugees headed on foot for Tanzania's border with Rwanda on Thursday on the heels of 240,000 who have already crossed in the past five days.
"It's going pretty smoothly. I don't like to say it but it is now almost routine," said Anne Willem Bijleveld of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in the Tanzanian town of Ngara.

He said Tanzanian troops would start emptying Keza camp of some 5,000 refugees who had remained there and up to 100,000 more were on the road between the Rwandan border and the village of Nyakahura 90 km (55 miles) to the southeast.
Aid officials said they expected the first of the group of 100,000 Hutus to arrive at the border later on Thursday or on Friday.
Outside Benaco camp, the largest refugee camp in Tanzania before the mass exodus started on Saturday, a column of ragged refugees filed along the road to the Rusumo border crossing.
Some said they were angry with their leaders for telling them to escape deeper into Tanzania after the Tanzanian government set a December 31 deadline for all 540,000 Rwandan refugees to return home.

Hundreds of thousands have been turned back by Tanzanian troops and police although large numbers are still hiding in the bush and some have even reached neighbouring Kenya and Malawi. The UNHCR says it is too early to say how many refugees are missing.
"I am very angry. Our leaders made a mistake by telling us to leave the camp. Before the (Tanzanian) government promised transport. Now we have to walk home," said LKeonard Kabera, 52.

"I started out from Lumasi camp and then I walked to Kitali and now I'm heading back from Kitali to Rwanda. My wife and six children are completely tired," said Kabera, adding they had been walking up and down the road for more than five days.
He said they had run out of food and had no money left.

The move last week deeper into Tanzania was led by former Rwandan Hutu Interahamwe militiamen and troops who refuse to go home because they risk being jailed for their roles in the 1994 genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
Tanzanian troops and police aided by a helicopter are searching for the missing hardliners, who had intimidated other refugees against returning but lost their hold over many on the road.
UNHCR spokesman Paul Stromberg said 30,000 crossed to Rwanda on Wednesday, taking the total since Saturday to nearly 240,000.
UNHCR staff checking for dead refugees in Benaco camp on Wednesday were startled to find 28 Rwandans at a church who said they would not return home until they received orders from God.
The East African Standard newspaper in Nairobi said on Thursday that at least 100 Rwandan Hutu refugees from Tanzania had secretly crossed into Kenya in the previous four days.
It said those who sneaked into Kenya used forged Tanzanian passports and entry documents and travelled on buses and taxis.
A UNHCR representative said between 80 and 100 suspected Rwandans reached Malawi from Tanzania in the last two weeks.

But Foreign Minister George Ntafu said Malawi would not offer asylum to Rwandans escaping repatriation from Zaire or Tanzania and accused UNHCR of breaking its promises to restore the environment after Mozambican refugees had harmed it.
